idiom_name: token bucket in a fixed struct over clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC), guarded by a pthread_mutex_t
implementation_notes: C provides no rate-limiting primitive, so the classic structure is hand-written: a struct holding the token count, the configured refill rate and burst ceiling and the timestamp of the last refill, plus a pthread_mutex_t that makes check-and-decrement atomic. Each decision reads CLOCK_MONOTONIC with clock_gettime - the manual describes it as the clock not affected by discontinuous jumps of the system time, which is exactly what interval accounting needs - refills by elapsed time capped at the burst, then either consumes a token or returns a refusal the caller maps to a 429-style response; for pacing rather than shedding the same deficit is converted into a nanosleep interval. Where the limit belongs to the infrastructure rather than the application, Linux traffic control shapes and polices at the socket layer and no in-process state exists at all.
pitfalls: Using CLOCK_REALTIME or gettimeofday makes the limiter wrong across NTP steps and manual clock changes; CLOCK_MONOTONIC is the interval clock.
The refill and decrement must both happen under the mutex, or two threads admit on the same token.
The refill must be capped at the burst ceiling; uncapped accumulation turns an idle period into an unlimited initial burst.
nanosleep is interruptible (EINTR) and coarse; a pacing loop must recompute the deficit after each wake-up instead of sleeping once.
